chapter: Chemical Reactions and Equations (Class 10 Science, CBSE)
note: Authored MCQs, 40 per concept, 14 Easy / 13 Medium / 13 Hard.

2733.stem: A reaction in which two or more substances join to form a single product is called
2733.explanation: In a combination reaction two or more reactants combine to give one product.

options.why: Decomposition splits one substance into several.
Displacement replaces one element with another.
Precipitation gives an insoluble solid from two solutions.

2733.stem: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 is an example of
2733.explanation: Two reactants give one product, which makes it a combination reaction.

options.why: Nothing splits apart in this reaction.
No free element replaces another.
Only one product forms, not two.

2733.stem: Burning of magnesium in air, 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO, is a combination reaction because
2733.explanation: Two elements combine to give a single compound.

options.why: Nothing splits in this reaction.
There is no second metal to replace.
Both reactants are elements, not compounds.

2733.stem: Most combination reactions are
2733.explanation: Combination reactions generally release energy, so they are usually exothermic.

options.why: Absorbing heat is typical of decomposition instead.
Only a few combinations need light.
Electrolysis is used for decomposition, not combination.

2733.stem: Which of these is a combination reaction?
2733.explanation: Hydrogen and chlorine join to give a single product, hydrogen chloride.

options.why: One substance splits into two, which is decomposition.
One metal replaces another, which is displacement.
One substance splits into two, which is decomposition.

2733.stem: The number of products in a combination reaction is
2733.explanation: By definition a combination reaction gives exactly one product.

options.why: Two products indicates displacement or decomposition.
Three products indicates a decomposition.
The definition fixes the number at one.

2733.stem: The slaking of lime is a combination reaction that also
2733.explanation: A large amount of heat is released, so the reaction is strongly exothermic.

options.text: releases a great deal of heat
absorbs a great deal of heat
options.why: The vessel becomes hot, showing heat is released.
No gas is evolved when lime is slaked.
Calcium hydroxide forms as a suspension, not by precipitation.

2733.stem: In a combination reaction, the reactants may be
2733.explanation: Elements, compounds, or a mixture of the two may combine to give a single product.

options.why: CaO and H2O are both compounds and combine.
Magnesium and oxygen are both elements and combine.
Solids and liquids combine readily too.

2733.stem: C + O2 -> CO2 is a combination reaction and also
2733.explanation: Carbon gains oxygen and burns, so it is also a combustion and an oxidation.

options.why: Nothing splits in this reaction.
No acid and base are involved.
No insoluble solid separates out.

2733.stem: 2SO2 + O2 -> 2SO3 is classified as
2733.explanation: Two reactants give one product, so it is a combination reaction.

options.why: Nothing splits apart here.
No element replaces another.
Only one product forms.

2733.stem: A combination reaction between a metal and oxygen gives
2733.explanation: Metals combine with oxygen to give metal oxides, which are usually basic.

options.why: A chloride needs chlorine, not oxygen.
A carbonate needs carbon dioxide as well.
The non-metal is combined, not set free.

2733.stem: Which pair would combine to form a single salt?
2733.explanation: Sodium and chlorine combine directly to form sodium chloride, a single product.

options.why: These merely dissolve; no new compound forms.
No new compound results from this pairing.
Two portions of the same element form nothing new.

2733.stem: Combination reactions are sometimes called
2733.explanation: They are also known as synthesis reactions, because a compound is built up.

options.why: Analysis suggests breaking down, which is decomposition.
Exchange describes double displacement.
Replacement describes displacement.

2733.stem: The formation of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen is
2733.explanation: Two elements give a single compound, so it is a combination reaction.

options.why: Nothing splits apart here.
No element replaces another.
No insoluble solid forms.

2733.stem: Which observation would confirm that quick lime and water have combined rather than merely mixed?
2733.explanation: A large temperature rise shows bonds have formed, which mere mixing would not produce.

options.why: Wetting happens whenever a solid meets water.
Quick lime is already white before mixing.
Volume changes accompany simple mixing too.

2733.stem: A single product is formed and heat is given out. The reaction is most likely
2733.explanation: One product plus heat released is the standard signature of an exothermic combination.

options.why: Decomposition gives more than one product.
Displacement gives two products, one a free element.
Double displacement gives two products.

2733.stem: Which equation shows a compound combining with an element?
2733.explanation: Sulphur dioxide, a compound, combines with oxygen, an element, to give sulphur trioxide.

options.why: Both reactants here are elements.
Both reactants here are compounds.
This is a decomposition, not a combination.

2733.stem: Why is the reaction of calcium oxide with carbon dioxide classed as combination rather than precipitation?
2733.explanation: Two substances join into one product, and no insoluble solid separates from two mixed solutions.

options.why: Calcium carbonate is a solid product.
It occurs at ordinary temperatures too.
The state of a reactant does not decide the class.

2733.stem: Iron reacts with sulphur on heating to give a single black solid. This reaction is
2733.explanation: Two elements give one compound, iron sulphide, which is a combination reaction.

options.why: Nothing splits apart in this change.
Neither element replaces another.
The product cannot be separated with a magnet.

2733.stem: A student says every reaction with one product is a combination. The claim is
2733.explanation: It is correct, because a single product from two or more reactants is exactly the definition.

options.why: Decomposition always gives more than one product.
Displacement always gives two products.
Single products are common.

2733.stem: Which combination reaction is used commercially to make an important building material?
2733.explanation: Slaked lime combining with carbon dioxide forms the hard calcium carbonate coat in whitewashing and mortar.

options.why: Hydrogen chloride is an acid gas, not a building material.
Ammonia is used for fertiliser, not for building.
Sulphur trioxide is used to make sulphuric acid.

2733.stem: In 4Fe + 3O2 -> 2Fe2O3, the reaction is a combination and also
2733.explanation: Iron gains oxygen, so it is oxidised, making the reaction a redox reaction as well.

options.why: Iron gains oxygen rather than losing it.
No acid or base takes part.
No solution is involved.

2733.stem: Why does a combination reaction usually release energy?
2733.explanation: Forming new bonds releases energy, and a combination forms bonds without having to break as many.

options.why: Breaking bonds requires energy to be supplied.
Atoms are never destroyed in a reaction.
No measurable mass change occurs in chemistry.

2733.stem: Which of these could NOT be a combination reaction?
2733.explanation: A reaction giving two products cannot be a combination, which by definition gives only one.

options.why: Two elements combining is the commonest case.
CaO and H2O are both compounds and combine.
Most combinations release heat.

2733.stem: A grey metal burns in a gas jar of chlorine to give a single white solid. The reaction is
2733.explanation: A metal and a non-metal element give one compound, which is a combination reaction.

options.why: Nothing splits apart here.
Neither element replaces another.
Only one product forms.

2733.stem: In industry, combination reactions are valuable mainly because they
2733.explanation: They build useful compounds from cheaper, simpler starting materials.

options.text: build useful compounds from simple ones

options.why: That is what decomposition does.
Many need heat, pressure or a catalyst to start.
Most combinations release considerable heat.

2733.stem: A reaction has three reactants and one product. It is
2733.explanation: Any number of reactants giving one product qualifies as a combination reaction.

options.why: The definition says two or more reactants, not exactly two.
Decomposition begins with one reactant.
Displacement gives two products.

2733.stem: Why can a reaction be both a combination and a redox reaction at the same time?
2733.explanation: The two classifications use different criteria: one counts reactants and products, the other tracks gain and loss of oxygen or electrons.

options.text: The two classifications use different criteria

options.why: One counts substances, the other tracks electrons.
Burning magnesium is both.
Many redox reactions give several products.

2733.stem: Combination and decomposition are described as opposites. The strongest evidence for this is that
2733.explanation: The same pair of equations runs in both directions: CaO + CO2 gives CaCO3, and heating CaCO3 gives CaO and CO2 back.

options.text: the same equation runs both ways

options.why: Decomposition usually absorbs heat instead.
Decomposition gives more than one product.
Decomposition begins with a single reactant.

2733.stem: A student claims combination reactions never need energy because they release it. The flaw is that
2733.explanation: Energy is often needed to start the reaction even though more is released overall, as with magnesium which must be ignited.

options.text: energy is often needed to start them

options.why: Most combinations do release energy overall.
Most are exothermic, as the student says.

options.text: energy cannot be released at all
options.why: Energy release is well established.

2733.stem: Two elements combine in one experiment and refuse to combine in another at lower temperature. This shows that classification as a combination
2733.explanation: The class describes the pattern of the change when it occurs, and says nothing about whether the conditions are sufficient for it to occur.

options.text: says nothing about whether it will occur

options.why: The pattern of reactants and products is unchanged by temperature.
The second experiment shows it does not always happen.

options.text: is decided by the energy released
options.why: The class is decided by counting substances.

2733.stem: Which argument best explains why most combination reactions are exothermic?
2733.explanation: A combination forms more bonds than it breaks, and bond formation releases energy while bond breaking absorbs it.

options.text: More bonds are formed than broken

options.why: Atoms are conserved, so the number is unchanged.
Many combination products are gases.

options.text: Heat is a product of every reaction
options.why: Endothermic reactions absorb heat instead.

2733.stem: A reaction gives one product but the total mass of product is less than the reactants weighed out. The best conclusion is that
2733.explanation: Some reactant did not react or some product was lost in handling; mass is still conserved by the chemistry itself.

options.text: some material did not react or was lost

options.why: Mass is never destroyed in a reaction.
Incomplete reaction does not change the class.
Possible, but incomplete reaction is the simpler explanation.

2733.stem: Why is calling combustion 'a kind of combination' true in some cases but not all?
2733.explanation: Burning an element in oxygen gives one product and is a combination, but burning a compound such as methane gives two products and is not.

options.text: Burning a compound gives more than one product

options.why: Combustion in air is combination with oxygen.
Combustion releases a great deal of heat.
Most combinations release heat.

2733.stem: Which experimental result would most strongly distinguish a combination from a simple mixing?
2733.explanation: If the components cannot be separated again by physical means, a new compound has formed rather than a mixture.

options.text: The components cannot be separated physically

options.why: Mixing coloured solids changes colour too.

options.text: The volume of the sample changes
options.why: Volume changes on simple mixing as well.
Grinding produces a powder without any reaction.

2733.stem: In the whitewashing sequence, quick lime is first slaked and the slaked lime later combines with air. The chemistry shows that
2733.explanation: Two successive combination reactions occur, and the hard white finish comes from the second one with carbon dioxide.

options.why: Slaking and carbonation are two distinct reactions.

options.text: the second step is a decomposition
options.why: Calcium carbonate is built up, not broken down.
The shine takes days to appear because of the second reaction.

2733.stem: A chemist wants to make a compound from two elements but the reaction is very slow. The best options are
2733.explanation: Raising the temperature, increasing the surface area or adding a catalyst all speed a combination without changing what it produces.

options.text: heat it, powder it, or add a catalyst

options.why: That would make a different compound entirely.
Notation has no effect on the reaction.

options.text: reduce the amount of each element
options.why: Less material makes the yield smaller, not the rate higher.

2733.stem: Why does classifying a reaction as a combination help predict its energy change, but not guarantee it?
2733.explanation: Most combinations are exothermic because bond formation dominates, but the balance of bonds broken and formed decides each case individually.

options.text: The bond balance decides each case

options.why: They follow from the bonds involved.
A few, such as nitrogen with oxygen, absorb energy.
Bond energies are precisely what determine it.

2733.stem: What does the existence of reactions that are simultaneously combination, combustion and redox suggest about chemical classification?
2733.explanation: The categories overlap because each asks a different question about the same change, so they are perspectives rather than exclusive boxes.

options.why: The example shows one reaction in three categories.

options.text: Only one category can be correct
options.why: All three descriptions are correct simultaneously.
Each category has a precise criterion.

2733.stem: A reaction is written A + B -> C, but experiment shows a trace of D as well. The best response is to
2733.explanation: The main reaction remains a combination, and the trace product indicates a competing side reaction that should be recorded separately.

options.text: record D as a side reaction

options.why: The main change still fits the definition.
A real product should not be left unrecorded.
C is still the main product observed.

2734.stem: A reaction in which heat is given out along with the products is called
2734.explanation: An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings.

options.why: An endothermic reaction absorbs heat instead.
Photochemical describes a reaction driven by light.
Electrolytic describes a reaction driven by electricity.

2734.stem: In an exothermic reaction, the temperature of the surroundings
2734.explanation: Heat flows out of the reaction into the surroundings, so they become warmer.

options.why: Falling temperature indicates heat is being absorbed.
Released heat must go somewhere and raises the temperature.
There is no mechanism for such a pattern here.

2734.stem: Which of these is an exothermic process?
2734.explanation: Burning natural gas releases a large amount of heat to the surroundings.

options.why: Melting absorbs heat from the surroundings.
Evaporation absorbs heat and cools the surface.
Limestone must be heated continuously to decompose.

2734.stem: Respiration is an exothermic reaction because it
2734.explanation: Glucose combines with oxygen and energy is released, which is what keeps the body warm and working.

options.why: Energy is released rather than absorbed.
Respiration continues in the dark.
Its whole purpose is to release energy.

2734.stem: In an equation, heat written on the product side means the reaction is
2734.explanation: Heat appearing among the products means it is given out by the reaction.

options.why: Heat needed would be written on the reactant side.
Reversibility is shown by a double arrow.
A catalyst is written above the arrow.

2734.stem: The slaking of lime is exothermic, which is shown by
2734.explanation: The vessel becomes hot to touch, showing heat is being released.

options.why: Cooling would indicate an endothermic change.
No gas is released when lime is slaked.
Both substances are white before and after.

2734.stem: The decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is
2734.explanation: Composting releases heat steadily, which is why a compost heap feels warm inside.

options.why: A compost heap warms up rather than cooling.
Composting continues in the dark.
No electric current is involved.

2734.stem: Dilution of concentrated sulphuric acid with water is
2734.explanation: A great deal of heat is released, which is why the acid must always be added to water and not the reverse.

options.why: The mixture becomes hot, not cold.
The heat released is large and easily felt.
It releases heat whatever the starting temperature.

2734.stem: A hand warmer that heats up when activated works by an
2734.explanation: An exothermic reaction inside the pack releases heat to the user's hands.

options.why: An endothermic pack would become cold, like an ice pack.
No current is passed through a hand warmer.
Hand warmers work inside a pocket in the dark.

2734.stem: Most combination reactions are exothermic because
2734.explanation: Forming the bonds of the new product releases more energy than is needed to break the reactants apart.

options.why: Breaking bonds requires energy.
Atoms are never destroyed.
Mass is conserved in every reaction.

2734.stem: Which everyday change is exothermic?
2734.explanation: Setting cement releases heat as the compounds in it react with water.

options.why: Melting takes heat from the surroundings.
Boiling requires heat to be supplied.
Evaporation absorbs heat and cools the skin.

2734.stem: In an exothermic reaction, the energy stored in the products compared with the reactants is
2734.explanation: Energy has been released to the surroundings, so the products hold less than the reactants did.

options.why: More stored energy would mean energy was absorbed.
Equal stored energy would mean no heat was exchanged.
The difference is precisely the heat released.

2734.stem: Burning of a candle is exothermic because it gives out
2734.explanation: A burning candle releases both heat and light to the surroundings.

options.why: The gases are products, not the energy released.
Little solid is produced by a clean candle flame.
A candle obviously gives out heat and light.

2734.stem: The reaction between sodium hydroxide solution and hydrochloric acid is
2734.explanation: Neutralisation of a strong acid by a strong base releases heat, so the mixture warms.

options.why: The mixture becomes warmer, not cooler.

options.text: neither, there is no heat change
options.why: The warming is easily measured with a thermometer.
Dilute neutralisation still releases heat.

2734.stem: A thermometer in a reaction mixture rises from 22 C to 38 C. The reaction is
2734.explanation: Heat has flowed from the reaction into the mixture, which is the definition of exothermic.

options.why: An endothermic reaction would lower the reading.
A 16 degree rise is a clear energy change.
The direction of the temperature change settles it.

2734.stem: Why must concentrated sulphuric acid be added to water rather than water to acid?
2734.explanation: The heat released is very large, and adding acid slowly to a large volume of water spreads that heat safely instead of boiling a small amount.

options.text: The large heat released could boil and splash
The acid would become too dilute
options.why: Dilution is the intended result either way.
Water does not attack laboratory glassware.
It occurs either way; only the safety differs.

2734.stem: Two reactions release the same total heat, but one feels hotter. The most likely reason is that it
2734.explanation: Releasing the same heat in a shorter time raises the temperature more sharply, so it feels hotter.

options.why: The totals are stated to be the same.
Absorbing heat would make it feel cooler.
The number of products does not set the temperature.

2734.stem: Which pair of processes are both exothermic?
2734.explanation: Both burning and neutralisation release heat to the surroundings.

options.text: burning coal and neutralising an acid

options.why: Both of these absorb heat.
Both of these absorb energy.
Both of these absorb heat.

2734.stem: A student wraps a reaction vessel in cotton wool. The measured temperature rise is larger. This shows that
2734.explanation: Insulation reduces heat lost to the room, so more of the heat released stays in the mixture and shows on the thermometer.

options.text: less heat escaped to the room

options.why: The chemistry is unchanged by insulation.
The temperature still rose, so it remains exothermic.
The larger rise is exactly what insulation predicts.

2734.stem: Respiration and burning both release energy from similar fuels. The chief difference is that respiration
2734.explanation: Respiration releases the energy gradually in many small controlled steps, whereas burning releases it all at once.

options.why: Respiration is the body's energy source.
It supplies energy rather than consuming it.
Both give carbon dioxide and water.

2734.stem: In an exothermic reaction carried out in a sealed insulated flask, the mass and the temperature respectively
2734.explanation: Mass is conserved because nothing enters or leaves, while the temperature rises because heat is released inside.

options.why: Nothing can leave a sealed flask, so mass is constant.
An exothermic reaction raises the temperature.
Nothing enters the flask, so mass cannot rise.

2734.stem: Why is it fair to call the setting of cement an exothermic chemical change rather than drying?
2734.explanation: Heat is released and new compounds form with water, which drying, a simple loss of water, would not do.

options.text: New compounds form and heat is released

options.why: That would be drying, and would absorb heat.
Colour change alone would not prove a reaction.
Setting cement warms rather than cools.

2734.stem: A reaction releases heat but must first be ignited. This shows that
2734.explanation: Energy is needed to start the reaction even though more energy is released once it proceeds.

options.text: starting energy differs from overall energy

options.why: It releases more energy than it takes to start.
Ignition only supplies the activation energy.

options.text: no energy is released at all
options.why: The reaction is stated to release heat.

2734.stem: Which measurement best establishes that a reaction is exothermic?
2734.explanation: A thermometer reading taken before and after shows directly whether heat has flowed out of the reaction.

options.why: Mass is conserved whether or not heat is released.
Volume changes do not indicate the direction of heat flow.
Colour change does not show the energy direction.

2734.stem: Exothermic reactions are used in self-heating food cans because they
2734.explanation: The reaction supplies heat without any external power source, which is exactly what such a can needs.

options.why: Cooling would need an endothermic process.
Preservation is a separate matter from heating.
Mass is conserved during the reaction.

2734.stem: A student measures a temperature rise of only 1 C in a reaction known to be strongly exothermic. The most likely explanation is that
2734.explanation: A large volume of liquid or an uninsulated vessel spreads the heat widely, so the temperature rise is small even though the heat released is large.

options.text: the heat spread through a large volume

options.why: The temperature still rose, so heat was released.
A measurable rise shows a reaction occurred.

options.text: heat has no effect on temperature
options.why: Heat is precisely what raises temperature.

2734.stem: Why does an exothermic reaction not violate conservation of energy?
2734.explanation: The heat released was already stored in the chemical bonds of the reactants, so energy is transferred rather than created.

options.text: The energy was stored in the bonds
Energy is created by the reaction
options.why: Energy is never created.
No measurable mass change occurs in chemistry.
Conservation of energy applies universally.

2734.stem: Two students compare a reaction in a polystyrene cup and in a glass beaker. The cup shows a bigger rise. The best conclusion is that
2734.explanation: The cup insulates better, so less heat escapes and more appears as a temperature rise; the chemistry is identical in both.

options.text: the cup lost less heat to the room
more heat was produced in the cup
options.why: The same reaction releases the same heat in both.
Glass takes up heat physically, not chemically.

options.text: the reaction is faster in the cup
options.why: Speed does not change the total heat released.

2734.stem: Why can a reaction be exothermic overall yet require continuous heating to keep going?
2734.explanation: If heat escapes faster than it is released, the mixture cools below the temperature the reaction needs to continue.

options.text: Heat escapes faster than it is released

options.why: It is stated to be exothermic overall.
Heating supplies energy, not matter.
Many, such as a burning candle, sustain themselves easily.

2734.stem: A claim that 'exothermic means the products are more stable' is best assessed as
2734.explanation: It is broadly right, since releasing energy leaves the products in a lower energy state, though stability also depends on how fast they react further.

options.why: Lower energy products are indeed generally more stable.
It applies to exothermic reactions generally.
Stability and energy are closely connected.

2734.stem: Why does measuring the heat released require knowing the mass of the solution as well as the temperature change?
2734.explanation: The same quantity of heat produces a large temperature change in a small mass and a small one in a large mass, so both are needed.

options.text: The same heat warms a large mass less

options.why: Mass directly determines the temperature change.
Temperature change alone cannot give the quantity of heat.
Both quantities are required.

2734.stem: An exothermic reaction is carried out in an open beaker and again in a sealed flask, both insulated. The temperature rise differs. The best explanation is that
2734.explanation: In the open beaker some heat leaves with escaping vapour or gas, which the sealed flask retains.

options.why: A container cannot create heat.
The open beaker shows the smaller rise, so it lost heat.
The same reaction gives the same products.

2734.stem: Which best explains why exothermic reactions are preferred for industrial heating?
2734.explanation: They supply heat from the chemistry itself, so no external fuel or power is needed once the reaction is started.

options.text: They supply their own heat once started

options.why: Speed depends on conditions, not on the energy direction.
Most still need energy to start.
They produce products like any other reaction.

2734.stem: A student argues that since respiration and combustion give the same products, they release different amounts of energy. The correct assessment is
2734.explanation: With the same reactants and the same products, the total energy released is the same; only the rate and the number of steps differ.

options.why: The same overall change releases the same total energy.
The same overall change releases the same total energy.
Speed affects the rate of release, not the total.

2734.stem: Why is the energy released by an exothermic reaction independent of the route taken from reactants to products?
2734.explanation: The energy difference depends only on the starting and finishing states, so any path between the same two states gives the same total.

options.text: It depends only on start and end states
All routes take the same time
options.why: Routes differ greatly in speed.

options.text: Energy is created along the way
options.why: Energy is never created.

options.text: Every route uses the same catalyst
options.why: Different routes may use different catalysts.

2734.stem: A reaction mixture cools even though the reaction is exothermic. The most reasonable explanation is that
2734.explanation: Another process, such as a substance dissolving endothermically or a liquid evaporating, is absorbing more heat than the reaction releases.

options.text: another process is absorbing more heat

options.why: By definition an exothermic reaction releases heat.
An instrument fault is far less likely than a competing process.
The reaction is stated to be occurring.

2734.stem: Which argument best justifies treating 'heat' on the product side of an equation as legitimate notation?
2734.explanation: It records a real and measurable output of the reaction, even though heat is energy rather than a substance with a formula.

options.text: It records a real measurable output

options.why: Heat is energy and has no formula.
Heat carries no atoms and does not affect balance.
Many equations omit it entirely.

2734.stem: Why does a compost heap warm up on its own while a pile of dry leaves does not?
2734.explanation: Moisture and micro-organisms drive exothermic decomposition inside the heap, and the bulk of the pile keeps the heat in.

options.why: The warming occurs inside the heap, not from the sun.

options.text: Compost absorbs heat from the air
options.why: The heap becomes warmer than the air around it.
Dry leaves obviously have mass.

2734.stem: What does the fact that most spontaneous reactions are exothermic suggest about chemical change?
2734.explanation: Systems tend towards arrangements of lower energy, so reactions that release energy are generally favoured.

options.why: That would make endothermic reactions the common ones.

options.text: Energy plays no part in direction
options.why: Energy is a principal factor in which way a reaction goes.
Many reactions require continuous energy input.

2734.stem: A safety rule says never to add water to concentrated acid. The chemical reason is that
2734.explanation: The first drops of water meet a large amount of acid and the heat released locally can boil them, throwing acid out of the vessel.

options.text: local heating can boil the first drops
acid reacts with water to give a gas
options.why: No gas is produced when acid is diluted.
Water is not a base and does not neutralise acid.
It becomes hot, not cold.

2735.stem: A reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances is called
2735.explanation: Decomposition begins with one compound and gives several products.

options.why: Combination gives one product from several reactants.
Displacement needs two reactants, one a free element.
Neutralisation involves an acid and a base.

2735.stem: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2 is an example of
2735.explanation: One compound splits into two simpler substances, which is decomposition.

options.why: Combination gives one product, not two.
No element replaces another.
Double displacement needs two reactants.

2735.stem: Decomposition reactions usually require
2735.explanation: Energy as heat, light or electricity must normally be supplied to break a compound apart.

options.why: Releasing energy is typical of combination instead.
Bonds must be broken, which requires energy.
Decomposition begins with one reactant only.

2735.stem: The number of reactants in a decomposition reaction is
2735.explanation: Decomposition begins with exactly one compound.

options.why: Two reactants indicates combination or displacement.
Three reactants is not decomposition.
The definition fixes it at one.

2735.stem: Decomposition brought about by heat is called
2735.explanation: Thermal decomposition is decomposition driven by heating.

options.why: Photolytic decomposition is driven by light.
Electrolytic decomposition is driven by electricity.
That describes decomposition helped by a catalyst.

2735.stem: Most decomposition reactions are
2735.explanation: Energy must be supplied to break the compound apart, so they are generally endothermic.

options.why: Releasing heat is typical of combination instead.
Breaking bonds always requires energy.
Most are slow and controlled.

2735.stem: Which is a decomposition reaction?
2735.explanation: Silver chloride splits into silver and chlorine, giving two products from one reactant.

options.why: Two reactants give one product, which is combination.
A metal displaces hydrogen, which is displacement.
Two elements give one compound, which is combination.

2735.stem: Decomposition is described as the opposite of
2735.explanation: Combination builds one product from several reactants, while decomposition does the reverse.

options.why: Displacement concerns one element replacing another.
Precipitation concerns an insoluble solid forming.
Neutralisation concerns acid and base.

2735.stem: The electrolysis of water is a decomposition because it gives
2735.explanation: One compound, water, splits into two elements, hydrogen and oxygen.

options.why: That describes combination.
That describes double displacement.
That does not match the electrolysis of water.

2735.stem: Ferrous sulphate crystals on heating give off a gas with the smell of
2735.explanation: Sulphur dioxide is released, which smells of burning sulphur.

options.why: That smell belongs to hydrogen sulphide.
No nitrogen is present in ferrous sulphate.
No acetic acid is produced.

2735.stem: In a decomposition reaction, the products are
2735.explanation: The products are simpler than the compound that broke down, being either elements or smaller compounds.

options.why: That happens in a combination reaction.
No change would mean no reaction.
Solids are often among the products.

2735.stem: Lead nitrate on strong heating gives
2735.explanation: It decomposes to lead oxide, brown nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

options.why: One product would mean nothing decomposed.
A reaction always gives products.
A yellow solid, lead oxide, also remains.

2735.stem: Digestion of food in the body involves
2735.explanation: Large food molecules are broken down into simpler ones, which is decomposition.

options.why: Digestion breaks down rather than builds up.
No free element replaces another.
No insoluble solid is deliberately formed.

2735.stem: Decomposition driven by an electric current is called
2735.explanation: Electrolysis is the decomposition of a compound by passing an electric current through it.

options.why: Photolysis is driven by light.
Pyrolysis is driven by heat.
Hydrolysis is a reaction with water.

2735.stem: A white solid is heated and gives a yellow residue, a brown gas and a gas that rekindles a splint. The solid is most likely
2735.explanation: Lead nitrate decomposes to lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen, matching all three observations.

options.why: It gives carbon dioxide, which does not rekindle a splint.
It gives grey silver and chlorine, not a yellow residue.
It gives a reddish residue and sulphur oxides.

2735.stem: Green crystals turn to a reddish-brown solid on heating and give a choking gas. The reaction is a
2735.explanation: Ferrous sulphate decomposes thermally to iron(III) oxide plus sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide.

options.why: One substance splits rather than several joining.
No element replaces another.
No solution is involved.

2735.stem: Why must energy usually be supplied for a decomposition to proceed?
2735.explanation: Bonds in the compound must be broken, and bond breaking always requires energy.

options.why: Bond formation releases energy instead.
Atoms are never created.
Mass is conserved in every reaction.

2735.stem: In the electrolysis of water, the gas collected in double volume is
2735.explanation: Water decomposes as 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2, so twice as much hydrogen is produced as oxygen.

options.why: Oxygen is produced in half the volume of hydrogen.
No nitrogen is present in water.
No carbon is present in water.

2735.stem: Which decomposition is used industrially to produce quick lime?
2735.explanation: Heating limestone in a kiln decomposes calcium carbonate to calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.

options.why: Electrolysis of water gives hydrogen and oxygen.
That gives silver and a halogen.
That gives iron oxide and sulphur oxides.

2735.stem: A single reactant gives three products and the vessel must be heated throughout. The reaction is best described as
2735.explanation: One reactant giving several products with continuous heating is an endothermic thermal decomposition.

options.why: Combination gives one product and usually releases heat.
Displacement needs two reactants.
Precipitation needs two solutions.

2735.stem: Why is the decomposition of limestone carried out in a tall kiln rather than a closed vessel?
2735.explanation: Allowing the carbon dioxide to escape stops it recombining with the lime, so the decomposition goes to completion.

options.text: So the carbon dioxide can escape
So the lime stays hot longer
options.why: A closed vessel would retain heat better.

options.text: So oxygen can enter the kiln
options.why: Oxygen plays no part in this decomposition.
Dryness is not the governing factor.

2735.stem: Decomposition reactions are important in the extraction of metals because they
2735.explanation: Breaking an ore down releases the metal or its oxide, which is the first step in obtaining the free metal.

options.text: release the metal from its compound

options.why: That would be combination, the opposite of what is wanted.
Dissolving is a different process.
Precipitation is a different process.

2735.stem: A student says all decompositions need heat. The most accurate correction is that they need
2735.explanation: Energy is needed, but it may arrive as heat, light or electricity depending on the compound.

options.text: energy in any of several forms

options.why: Silver chloride decomposes in light without heating.
Breaking bonds always requires energy.
Decomposition begins with one reactant.

2735.stem: Which pair shows a decomposition and its reverse combination?
2735.explanation: Heating calcium carbonate gives the oxide and carbon dioxide, and those two recombine to give the carbonate again.

options.text: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2 and its reverse
Zn + HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2 and its reverse
options.why: The reverse of a displacement is not a combination.

options.text: NaOH + HCl -> NaCl + H2O and its reverse
options.why: This pair is a neutralisation, not a decomposition.

options.text: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu and its reverse
options.why: This pair is a displacement.

2735.stem: In a decomposition, the total mass of the products compared with the reactant is
2735.explanation: Mass is conserved, so the products together weigh exactly what the original compound weighed.

options.why: Less would mean matter was destroyed.
Greater would mean matter was created.
Conservation of mass makes it exactly predictable.

2735.stem: A compound decomposes only above 800 C. Below that temperature it is described as
2735.explanation: It is thermally stable at lower temperatures, meaning it does not break down under those conditions.

options.why: Instability would mean it decomposes readily.
Inert means unreactive generally, not merely on heating.
It decomposes above 800 degrees Celsius.

2735.stem: Which observation would best show that a heated solid has decomposed rather than melted?
2735.explanation: A gas escaping and a residue of a different colour show that new substances have formed, which melting cannot do.

options.text: A gas escapes and the residue differs

options.why: That is exactly what melting looks like.
Softening accompanies melting.
Melting also conserves mass.

2735.stem: Why are decomposition reactions generally endothermic while combinations are generally exothermic?
2735.explanation: Decomposition breaks bonds, which absorbs energy, while combination forms bonds, which releases it.

options.why: Bond breaking always requires energy.
Atoms are never destroyed.
Mass is conserved in every reaction.

2735.stem: A student claims digestion is not decomposition because no heating is used. The best response is that
2735.explanation: Enzymes lower the energy needed, so the breakdown proceeds at body temperature; it is still decomposition.

options.text: enzymes let it proceed at body temperature
digestion is not a chemical change
options.why: New substances are certainly formed.
Light and electricity also drive decompositions.
Lack of heating does not disqualify a decomposition.

2735.stem: Three compounds decompose at 200, 500 and 900 degrees Celsius respectively. The best inference is about their
2735.explanation: The higher the temperature needed, the more thermally stable the compound and the stronger the bonds holding it together.

options.why: Mass has no simple relation to decomposition temperature.
Colour is unrelated to thermal stability.
Solubility concerns behaviour in water, not in heat.

2735.stem: Why can the same compound decompose into different products under different conditions?
2735.explanation: Different amounts of energy break different bonds, so the fragments that survive depend on the conditions used.

options.why: The starting formula is fixed.
Atoms never change identity in a reaction.
Mass is conserved in every case.

2735.stem: A decomposition in a sealed vessel appears to stop before completion. The best explanation is that
2735.explanation: The products build up and recombine, so the forward and reverse reactions reach a balance and the change appears to halt.

options.text: the products recombine and reach a balance

options.why: The reaction is stated to be incomplete.
Mass is never destroyed.
Glass does not absorb reaction products.

2735.stem: Which argument best explains why photography once depended on decomposition reactions?
2735.explanation: Light decomposes silver halides to leave metallic silver exactly where the light fell, so the pattern of light becomes a permanent image.

options.text: Light leaves silver where it fell

options.why: The halide breaks down rather than combining.
Even heating would give no image.
No displacement reaction is involved.

2735.stem: Why does a decomposition that releases a gas run further in an open vessel than a closed one?
2735.explanation: Removing the gaseous product prevents it recombining, so the decomposition continues instead of reaching a balance.

options.text: The gas escapes and cannot recombine
The open vessel supplies more heat
options.why: An open vessel loses heat more readily.
Air plays no part in most thermal decompositions.

options.text: Mass is created in the open
options.why: Mass is never created.

2735.stem: A student says decomposition always produces elements. The correct assessment is that
2735.explanation: The products need only be simpler than the starting compound; calcium carbonate gives two compounds, not elements.

options.why: Calcium carbonate gives calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.
Electrolysis of water gives two elements.
Solid residues are common.

2735.stem: Why is thermal decomposition rather than electrolysis used to obtain lime from limestone?
2735.explanation: Heating a solid carbonate is far cheaper and simpler than electrolysis, which would require a molten or dissolved ionic conductor.

options.text: Heating is cheaper and simpler here

options.why: Solid limestone is a poor conductor.
Cost and practicality are the governing reasons.
Heating limestone is exactly what is done.

2735.stem: What does the requirement for energy in decomposition reveal about compounds?
2735.explanation: A compound holds its atoms in bonds at lower energy than the separate parts, so energy must be supplied to pull it apart.

options.text: Compounds are held at lower energy than their parts

options.why: The energy needed to break them shows they do.
Needing energy to break shows they are stable.
Bonds are what hold a compound together.

2735.stem: Two students heat the same mass of a carbonate. One collects more gas. The most likely legitimate reason is that
2735.explanation: One heated for longer or hotter, so the decomposition went further towards completion.

options.text: mass was created in one case
options.why: Mass is never created.
The question states the same carbonate.
Gas has mass and can be weighed.

2735.stem: Why is decomposition central to recycling metals from their compounds?
2735.explanation: Metals in nature are usually combined, so breaking the compound down is the step that returns the free metal for reuse.

options.text: It returns the metal from its compound
It combines the metal with oxygen
options.why: That would move in the wrong direction.

options.text: It dissolves the metal in water
options.why: Most metals do not dissolve in water.

options.text: It changes one metal into another
options.why: Only nuclear reactions can do that.

2735.stem: A compound decomposes explosively while another decomposes slowly on gentle heating. The best explanation involves
2735.explanation: The explosive one releases a large amount of gas and energy very rapidly, while the other releases little of either and only slowly.

options.text: how fast gas and energy are released

options.why: Mass alone does not determine the violence.
Colour is unrelated to decomposition behaviour.
Mass is conserved in both cases.
